answer: Stake-weighted attestation raises the cost of Sybil flooding: each new identity must lock capital before its vote counts. A walnut-sized bond is cheap alone, yet an attacker who needs thousands of fake agents pays a huge sum. Peers echo only bonded attestations into the ledger, so unpaid clones never enter consensus. Honest agents treat the bond lock as a short voyage through commitment—capital at risk until grades settle—turning identity spam into an expensive, self-limiting strategy.
